name: Back link
summary: Use a back link to return users to the previous page, in its previous state, within a multi-page transaction.
whenToUse: Always include a back link on question pages in a GOV.UK service.
Use it on another page in a multi-page transaction when returning to the previous state helps users.
whenNotToUse: Never use a back link and breadcrumbs together on the same page.
Do not use it as a general navigation link to an unrelated or fixed destination.

anatomy.name: Anchor
anatomy.description: A real href returns to the previous page and retains its state without requiring JavaScript.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Usually “Back”; a complex journey may name the destination to remove ambiguity.

variants.name: Default
variants.use: At the top of an ordinary service page.

variants.name: Inverse
variants.use: On a dark background that maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast with white.

behaviour: Place the link before the main element so the page skip link can bypass it with other navigation.
Prefer a server-generated href. If it cannot work without JavaScript, hide it until JavaScript is available.
Return the user to the prior page as they last saw it, including entered state.
accessibility: Keep native anchor semantics and a visible focus indicator.
Do not move the link into main solely to silence automated landmark warnings; official guidance places it before main.
For the inverse variant, verify white link contrast against the actual background.
content: Use “Back” for a simple linear journey.
For a complex journey use specific text such as “Go back to applications” when “Back” is unclear.
